docs.summary: Global knobs for a bake. Per-instance / per-target settings live on those objects.
Environment (sky) radiance returned when a ray misses everything. Used as the constant fallback when [`Environment`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.BakeOptions~Environment) is not set.

docs.summary:
Optional HDR environment: given a normalized ray direction (the direction the ray travels into the sky), returns the incoming radiance. Lets callers plug a cubemap/equirect sky as a GI source instead of the flat [`SkyColor`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.BakeOptions~SkyColor). When null, [`SkyColor`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.BakeOptions~SkyColor) is used.

**Thread-safety:** invoked concurrently from many bake worker threads; the callback must be pure / read-only (e.g. sampling immutable cubemap data).

When true, the lightmap includes direct lighting at the texel itself. When false, only the indirect contribution is stored: direct shadow rays at bounce hit points are *still* fired (so bounced light propagates correctly), but the texel's own direct lighting must be added at runtime by a dynamic-light shader. The standard "indirect-only baked lighting" pipeline.

This is the scene-wide form of [`BakeDirect`](#api~Prowl.Photonic.Scene.Lights.Light~BakeDirect), which does the same thing for one light. Setting this false is equivalent to clearing that flag on every light.

When true, all bake rays cull back faces, so light behaves as it does in a backface-culled rasterizer: it can pass up through a one-sided floor, the way Prowl's backface-culled shadows allow. When false the tracer is two-sided. The front-face winding is fixed to the renderer's convention by the integrator.

Indirect samples shot per texel per iteration. The bake is a progressive accumulator, so this paces it rather than deciding quality: total samples are iterations x this. Larger values mean coarser progress steps and slightly less per-iteration overhead.

Trace one texel per `SparseStride` x `SparseStride` cell of the atlas and interpolate the rest from the traced points around them. 1 traces every texel. 8 traces a few percent of an atlas, which converges dramatically faster at the cost of fine indirect detail. Contacts, corners and shadow boundaries keep their own points automatically, whatever this is set to.

Let sparse sampling cover direct lighting as well as indirect. Off by default: direct light is where the fast-changing detail lives, and interpolating it blurs every shadow edge by about one cell. It is also the cheap half of the bake, so leaving it dense costs little.

Edge dilation pixels applied after the bake, so filtering at a chart edge has something valid to read. 2 is the floor rather than a preference: bicubic lightmap sampling reads two texels past the chart, and anything less means it samples texels the bake never wrote.

Blend the two sides of every UV seam together after each iteration, so edges that are continuous on the model but split in the atlas stop showing a visible lighting discontinuity. Costs a pass over the seam texels per iteration.

Surface offset for ray origins, in world units. 0 derives it from the scene's size, which is the only way to be right at every scale: a millimetre is generous on a character, invisible on a terrain, and catastrophic on a scene modelled in centimetres. Ray origins additionally carry a magnitude-relative epsilon, so geometry far from the world origin stays separated regardless.
Maximum ray distance for visibility tests. 0 derives it from the scene bounds, which is what a fixed number can never track.
Cap on worker threads. -1 = use the runtime default.
Deterministic seed for the bake's PRNG. Two bakes with the same seed produce the same output.
Switches for diagnosing a bake. None of them improve output; they isolate causes.
